name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 18, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:06 p.m., on April
18, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 13, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor

City Council Minutes  1  April 18, 2011
   Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:06 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem Ury
was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council continued to give direction to staff
but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Arts Alive Festival Presentation

  Claudia Divito, Chairperson of the Cultural Arts Committee, discussed the activities
  planned for and the exhibitors participating in the 2011 Arts Alive event. The Council
  Members also viewed a short video from the 2010 Arts Alive festival.

P2.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners

  Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented Community Recycling Program
  Awards to Roberta Miller and Dan Kemp from the Valencia community, Anthony
  Constantino from the Arroyo Vista complex, Michael Bailey from the Casa Loma
  complex, and Mark Wilson from the California Terrace community.

P3.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Leckness presented Certificates of Commendation to Sergeant Camilo R. Osuna
  and Lance Corporal Deron J. Johnson.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dan Avery, M.V.: discussed the recent Tea Party demonstration at the corner of La Paz and
Marguerite and he stated that participants should be ashamed for displaying the confederate flag
during the event.

City Council Minutes  2  April 18, 2011
 Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: announced that the Orange County Workforce Investment Board is
sponsoring a free South Orange County Job Fair on May 11, 2011, at the Laguna Hills Mall. For
more information, residents can visit www.ocjobfair.org.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated March 25, 2011, in the amount of $2,457,273.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated April 1, 2011, in the amount of $645,236.06

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2011

  Received and filed.

6.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2011

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  April 18, 2011
 7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2011

  Received and filed.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

9.  Service Cost Recovery Study

  Treasury Manager Josephine Julian presented the staff report.

  Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing at 7:43 p.m.

  Sharon Cody, M.V.: asked staff and the City Council to reconsider fee increase for
  residents who wish to relinquish their own pets in these difficult economic times. She
  stated that if pet owners cannot afford to surrender their animals to the shelter and they
  cannot keep them, their dogs and cats will become strays on the road.

  Mayor Leckness closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to approve the
  recommended changes to the Library and Cultural Services fees and adopt Resolution
  11-23A Revising Certain Fees and Charges (Library and Cultural Services.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, and Leckness
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to approve the
  recommended changes to the Animal Services fees.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley
  NOES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the

City Council Minutes  4  April 18, 2011
   Animal Services Fees as proposed with the exception of the increase in relinquishment
  fees for residents.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Leckness
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to maintain the current schedule for Animal
  Services fees. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the recommended changes to the City Clerk fees and adopt Resolution 11-23B
  Revising Certain Fees and Charges (City Clerk.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the recommended changes to the Mission Viejo Television fees and adopt
  Resolution 11-23C Revising Certain Fees and Charges (Mission Viejo Television.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the recommended changes to the Parking Citation fees and adopt Resolution11-
  23D Revising Certain Fees and Charges (Parking Citation.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, and Leckness
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

City Council Minutes  5  April 18, 2011
 OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

10.  Internet Business Coupon Savings Program

  Deputy City Manager Karen Wylie presented the staff report.

  Steve Peters, Mission Viejo Locals Only, M.V.: discussed his company‟s qualifications
  and asked the City Council to consider awarding a contract to his firm.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: expressed support for the proposed coupon savings program.

  Donna Lang Stoffel, Massage Heights, M.V.: expressed support for a business coupon
  program.

  Dan Avery, M.V.: asked who will collect fees from the businesses if the program moves
  forward after the trial year.

  Shripathi Kamath, M.V.: presented a written comment in support of the proposed
  program.

  Council Member Reardon and Council Member Schlicht expressed an interest in
  receiving proposals from Mission Viejo web designers.

  Paula Gibbs, Mission Viejo Locals Only, M.V.: stated that the goal is to keep business
  local and she asked the Council to support her company‟s proposal.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) establish
  a Mission Viejo Internet Coupon Savings Program as a pilot program for 12-months; (2)
  approve the draft Professional Services Agreement for $3,300 with Victoria Alberty-
  deGoede; and (3) receive and file the report on the Internet Business Coupon Savings
  Program.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Leckness
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

City Council Minutes  6  April 18, 2011
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) establish
  a Mission Viejo Internet Coupon Savings Program as a pilot program for 12-months; (2)
  direct staff to issue a Request for Proposals for the Internet Business Coupon Savings
  Program; and (3) direct the City Attorney take an active part in making sure the RFP and
  subsequent agreement are legal.

  Mayor Leckness withdrew his second. The motion died for lack of a second.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Kelley

16.  Healthy Eating Active Living (HEAL) City Resolution

  Council Member Kelley presented her report.

  The following expressed support for the City's participation in the HEAL program: Tracy
  Bryars, M.V.; Carla DiCandia, representing Mission Hospital; and Jan Teitelbaum, M.V.

  Council Member Schlicht stated for the record that she is supportive of a healthy lifestyle
  but she is opposed to government‟s interference in that.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 11-24, as amended, Declaring Mission Viejo a Healthy Eating Active
  Living (HEAL) City; and (2) approve becoming a partner in the Move More Eat Healthy
  OC Campaign.

  Amendment to Resolution: change the wording in section 4 to say "the head of each
  affected City department should report back to the City Council annually..."

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, and Leckness
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

8.  Storm Drain and Water Quality Improvements for Oso Parkway (CIP 207)-
  Rejection of Bids

City Council Minutes  7  April 18, 2011
   Council Member Reardon asked if the bid rejection would delay the construction at Oso
  and Marguerite.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon replied that it will not delay the current project.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  reject all bids for the project; and (2) authorize staff to re-advertise for construction bids
  for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

2.  City Council Minutes

  Referring to the report of Closed Session on page 3 of the April 4 Minutes, Council
  Member Schlicht stated that she would like to reverse her vote on the Closed Session
  agenda item.

  City Attorney Curley responded that the Minutes from this meeting will reflect that
  Council Member Schlicht had a change of heart and she can further emphasize her
  position when the matter comes before the City Council for final action.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 4, 2001, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Leckness
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

11.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley announced that she will defer her report until the next meeting.

City Council Minutes  8  April 18, 2011
   Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: suggested that the City Council consider hiring an
  independent fire safety consultant to propose measures to reduce fire and paramedic costs
  without sacrificing quality services.

12.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury was absent therefore no report was given.

13.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing to report at this time.

14.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager's Report

City Manger Wilberg announced that he had nothing to report.

City Attorney's Report

City Attorney Curley announced that he had nothing to report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that memorial services for former resident and hometown
hero, Snuffy Brown, will be held on Wednesday, April 20, 2011, at 11:00 a.m. at Saddleback
Church. She also announced that she has organized a blood drive on April 19, 2011, at the
Murray Community and Senior Center from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. She encouraged residents to
donate blood as a way to make a difference in the lives of other people and to potentially save

City Council Minutes  9  April 18, 2011
 three lives. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at various events including the
Vocational Visions awards dinner where Mission Viejo was honored as Employer of the Year;
an egg decorating event at the Kaleidoscope shopping center; the YMCA Healthy Kids day; and
a presentation at Casta del Sol with guest speaker Chuck DeVore. Council Member Kelley
reminded residents that Bunny Days will be held on Saturday, April 23, 2011, at the Murray
Center and Oso Viejo Park and she reminded the community that this is “Turn off the TV” week.
The City of Mission Viejo is providing a variety of activities at the recreation centers to assist
families who participate in this national event. Council Member Kelley congratulated the two
Marines who were recognized earlier in the evening and she thanked them for their service. She
also expressed her appreciation to the Marine Adoption Committee for partnering with the City
to help these young men and women. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community
of Character word for the month of April is service.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon discussed a recent, very productive, meeting with City Engineer Rich
Schlesinger in preparation for her service on the South Orange County Watershed Management
Area Executive Committee. She also outlined her attendance at the Sheriff‟s Department Medal
of Valor luncheon. The men and women who received the Medal of Valor were very deserving
and she noted that she has a video of the event for anyone who is interested in watching it.
Council Member Reardon discussed her tour with Mission Viejo Code Enforcement officer
Karen Rottmann. Ms. Rottmann is very professional and did a wonderful job explaining areas of
concern and highlighting some of the properties that have been transformed. Council Member
Reardon announced that she received her new iPad from IT staff and she, and the other Council
Members, are learning to use the computers to view their Council Meeting agenda materials in
an effort to save money and resources. Ms. Reardon announced that she will be touring the
Marguerite Tennis Center soon and she looks forward to learning more about that facility. She
concluded her comments by reminding her colleagues and residents to keep two young children
with cancer, Cade and Kaylee, in their thoughts and prayers.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that her prayers are off to the eastern states that were stricken
with deadly tornados. She noted that as we enter holy week for Easter and Passover, the Council
Members should have good hopes and wishes for working together and for peace. Council
Member Schlicht reminded the community that Bunny Days will be held on Saturday, April 23
and she encouraged residents to attend and have fun. She discussed her recent visit to the grand
opening of Lennar‟s “The Ridge” condominiums and she observed that the floor plans are very
nice and well thought out. She also read a portion of an article from the National Library
Association regarding National Library Week. The article outlined the benefits of library
membership and she further noted that NPR wrote an editorial on the role of libraries alongside

City Council Minutes  10  April 18, 2011
 book stores and eBooks. She stated that the City needs to keep an eye on this and find some way
to maintain the library as a viable resource. Council Member Schlicht announced that she
attended the Tea Party on April 15. There was an enthusiastic crowd and a tremendous response
from drivers honking their horns as they passed by. She also announced that the Saddleback
Republican Assembly‟s featured guest speaker is Congressman Gary Miller and the event will be
held on Thursday, April 21, 2011, at 7:00 p.m. Council Member Schlicht thanked the Marines
and stated that she is so grateful for a City that supports them. She concluded her comments by
reading two quotes from Ronald Reagan: “The government's view of the economy could be
summed up in a few short phrases: If it moves, tax it. If it keeps moving, regulate it. And if it
stops moving, subsidize it” and "The nine most terrifying words in the English language are, „I'm
from the government and I'm here to help.‟”

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he attended a roast for Laguna Niguel Mayor Gary Capata and
he enjoyed being one of the roasters. He also attended a recent Chamber of Commerce black tie
event at the Dana Point Marriott. Mayor Leckness thanked City staff for repairing a huge pot
hole that was reported to him by a resident. He was impressed that the repair was made the same
day that he conveyed the information to staff. He also noted that he utilized the City‟s graffiti
hotline to report a curse word written on a wall and the graffiti was removed within 24 hours.
Mayor Leckness announced that he likes the new iPad and he is working to learn how to use it
with his Agenda materials.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:47 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Carroll "Snuffy" Brown, to Monday, May
2, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 2, 2011

City Council Minutes  11  April 18, 2011
